Q1: Dispatch Call A (Maple St, 7.8). Chest pain in a 68-year-old male is the highest-acuity call of the three and carries the greatest risk of rapid deterioration. The 9.0 threshold means none are critical, but that doesn't justify holding the unit — scores are a triage ranking, and A clearly leads, so the medic unit goes to Maple St.
Q2: Dispatch Call A (Pine Rd, 8.4). A kitchen fire is a working structure fire that can escalate and trap or injure occupants even with the family evacuated. The dumpster fire scores nearly as high but poses less immediate threat to life and property, so the engine goes to Pine Rd.
Q3: Dispatch Call A (1st St, 8.9). A reported trapped occupant with smoke showing is a life-safety incident that can become unsurvivable within minutes. An elevator rescue with two conscious occupants is urgent but stable by comparison, so the ladder truck goes to 1st St and elevator rescue can wait or be covered next.
Q4: Dispatch Call A (Hill Rd, 7.1). A diabetic emergency is a real medical incident requiring treatment; the event standby scores lower and is preventive, not an emergency. The BLS unit goes to Hill Rd.
Q5: Dispatch Call A (River St, 8.1). Difficulty breathing can deteriorate into respiratory arrest with little warning, so a breathing emergency outranks a hip injury even when scores are nearly tied. The medic unit goes to River St.
Q6: Dispatch Call B (Side St, 6.5) and request mutual aid for Call A. A brush fire near homes has growth and exposure risk that a vehicle fire with no occupants does not, so the engine's own coverage belongs to Side St. Take the mutual aid offer and send it to the vehicle fire on Main St so both calls are covered.
Q7: Dispatch Call A (Park Ave, 7.5). A multi-vehicle accident with injuries is exactly the kind of complex, multi-casualty scene a battalion chief exists to command. There are no competing calls, so the chief goes to Park Ave to establish command and oversight.
Q8: Dispatch Call A (Cedar Ln, 8.7). Stroke symptoms are time-critical with a closing treatment window — every minute of delay reduces the chance of a good outcome. Abdominal pain is serious but not immediately time-bound, so the medic unit goes to Cedar Ln.
Q9: Dispatch Call A (Summit Dr, 5.9). A gas leak is a genuine hazard requiring investigation and mitigation even at a moderate score, and the unit is idle with nothing else in the queue. There is no strategic reason to hold an available engine, so dispatch it to Summit Dr.
